p01.why: f names an overload set of two functions, which decltype cannot take.

p02.why: ref() is an lvalue of the abstract class A, so the result is A&, and the call is not evaluated.

p03.why: A non-static member can be named without an object in an unevaluated operand, and decltype gives its declared type int.

p04.why: a + b has the common type long, which is the trailing return type.

p05.why: The discarded expressions are evaluated in constant evaluation with no effect, and f() returns 1; any unused-value warning stays a warning.

p06.why: Access control still applies in an unevaluated operand, and m is private.

p07.why: Plain parameter names give their declared types const int& and int.

p08.why: No operand is evaluated, so count stays 0; bump is not declared noexcept, so n is false.

p09.why: The class prvalue in the expression statement becomes a temporary that is destroyed at once.

p10.why: The discarded name v reads a volatile object, which constant evaluation rejects, so the static_assert is not a constant expression.

p11.why: declared_only and make_big are used only in unevaluated operands, so they need no definition.

p12.why: decltype can name a base class in a base list.

p13.why: Each operand is an lvalue other than a plain name, so each result is int&.

p14.why: For decltype a call that gives a class prvalue can have an incomplete type.

p15.why: Enumerator names give their enumeration types E and F.

p16.why: A member access on a call that gives a class prvalue needs a complete class, and Inc is incomplete.

p17.why: Deleted functions are still checked in an unevaluated operand.

p18.why: The incomplete-type exception is for decltype only; sizeof of an incomplete type is not valid.

p19.why: A bit-field member access gives its declared type unsigned short.

p20.why: Plain names give the declared types with their references and qualifiers.

p21.why: Two int lvalues give an lvalue, so int&; with the prvalue 1 the result is a prvalue int.

p22.why: runtime() is not evaluated, so sizeof gives a constant sizeof(int).

p23.why: decltype(x) gives the variable's type int, and in a lambda that is not mutable decltype((x)) for a copy capture is const int&.

p24.why: Clang warns by default about the side effect in sizeof and -Werror makes it an error; GCC gives no warning and compiles.

p25.why: GCC accepts decltype in the qualified name of a member definition; Clang and EDG reject it.

p26.why: decltype(f()) is int and decltype(v) is int, so p points to v, which is 4.

p27.why: A single function name gives its function type int(int).

p28.why: A non-static member can be named without an object in sizeof, also from a nested class.

p29.why: A class prvalue keeps const, so const S; a non-class prvalue has no cv-qualifiers, so int.

p30.why: Member access without parentheses gives the declared type of the member, ignoring the const of s.

p31.why: All three discarded-value expressions are evaluated, so calls is 3.

p32.why: sizeof needs a usable destructor, and D's destructor is deleted.

p33.why: The cast is an xvalue giving int&&, S{}.m without parentheses gives the declared int, and (S{}.m) is an xvalue giving int&&.

p34.why: The types follow the usual arithmetic conversions and the page's conditional examples.

p35.why: m is a member of O, and I::g has no O object, so the evaluated use of m is not valid.

p36.why: A lambda can occur in the operand of decltype and sizeof.

p37.why: decltype of a structured binding gives the declared type of the data member, int.

p38.why: The call does not need the definition of W<int>, so the static_assert in W is never instantiated.

p39.why: never_defined is used only in sizeof, so it needs no definition.

p40.why: A discarded glvalue is not copied.

p41.why: x == 1; has no effect, so the compilers warn and -Werror makes it an error.

p42.why: For decltype a call giving a class prvalue needs no usable destructor, and the comma's right operand is that call.

p43.why: The volatile operand of + is read, and constant evaluation rejects the read.

p44.why: GCC rejects decltype after ~ in an explicit destructor call; Clang and EDG accept it.

p46.why: A cast to void stops the warning about the unused nodiscard result.

p47.why: 1 / z is not evaluated, so the division by zero does not matter.

p48.why: A string literal is an lvalue of type const char[3].

p49.why: f is an overload set with no target type to pick one function.

p50.why: i + 1, i++, f(), and 42 are prvalues of int, and g() is an int lvalue.

p51.why: decltype(s) can begin a qualified name for a member type and a static member.
